acceptance_criteria: A nonempty source containing one valid record larger than the byte window cannot return successful empty evidence; it yields a bounded oversized-record or incomplete observation outcome.

The reader returns a versioned bounded observation receipt containing availability, source size, read offset, bytes read, truncation, discarded-leading-fragment, complete-line count, observation time, and source generation without exposing source content or location.
A tail beginning inside a record reports the discarded fragment and still parses later complete records, including when the byte offset intersects a multibyte sequence.

Malformed JSON, valid non-object JSON, invalid shape, missing message, missing timestamp, invalid timestamp, unknown level, intentional suppression, and oversized record produce distinct bounded parser outcomes and aggregate counts.
Missing or invalid event timestamps remain unknown; observation time stays separately named and cannot substitute for event time without explicit provenance.
Unknown numeric and string severity remains fail-visible and cannot become info; projected severity and error-impact fields derive from one normalization result and cannot contradict each other.

The logs API returns a versioned envelope that distinguishes readable empty, nonempty with zero accepted records, incomplete, unavailable, and parser-degraded observations; no compatibility adapter may collapse those states to a valid empty array.
Feed loss diagnostics are episode-bounded and distinguish parser loss from intentional suppression without emitting one warning per rejected line.

Console log and operator surfaces display observation freshness, coverage, truncation, and rejected-record classes separately from accepted entry count and preserve explicit stale or unavailable state.

Property and fuzz tests cover arbitrary bounded offsets, record sizes, newline placement, multibyte boundaries, malformed shapes, timestamp variants, and severity values within fixed memory and time limits.
Self-heal, replay, and recovery consumers record whether log evidence was complete, incomplete, or unavailable; incomplete evidence alone cannot authorize a no-work or recovered conclusion.

All tests, fixtures, responses, diagnostics, review evidence, and receipts use reserved synthetic values and disclose no source content, filesystem location, identity, message, credential, process, or topology data.
blast_radius: Fleet log-file tailing, log-data and feed parsing, logs API compatibility, console log and operator rendering, timestamp and severity truth, realtime invalidation consumers, recovery decisions that treat absence as evidence, bounded parser diagnostics, and shared observation taxonomy coordination.
evidence_summary: Two identical GraphQL reads established the live issue node, title, body bytes and SHA-256, empty labels, URL, and timestamp. The local SSH tracking ref and exact SSH remote main both remained at the pinned revision. Every decisive source and test path is unchanged between that pin and the audit worktree. At the pin, readTailLinesDetailed reads at most the final 65,536 bytes from an arbitrary offset, decodes the buffer directly, filters split lines, and returns only ok plus lines; it exposes none of the requested coverage or fragment fields. The logs route silently skips every thrown parse or shape error, substitutes current time for missing or invalid event time, maps unknown numeric or nonnumeric severity to info, and returns a bare array. The feed parser returns the same null for malformed JSON, invalid or missing messages, declared noise, and ordinary suppressed information; its caller increments one suppressed counter for every null. It independently substitutes current time and maps an unknown numeric level to info while deriving isError from the raw threshold. The console API and UI accept only LogEntry arrays and therefore cannot render reader completeness or parser-loss provenance. A write-free in-memory canary through the real feed parser proved malformed input and intentional noise have the same result, an undated record receives observation time without a provenance field, and level 999 projects as info with isError true. A separate fail-closed pinned-source probe established the fixed window, absent receipt fields, bare-array response, parser-loss conflation, both timestamp fallbacks, severity fallback, and array-only console contract. A fully paginated all-state issue scan covered 518 issues in six pages and found adjacent but separately owned source lifecycle, response projection, client reconciliation, and realtime-poller cycle-health work rather than a duplicate owner. A fully paginated current open-pull-request scan covered 39 pull requests, 27 drafts, 43 changed-file pages, and 1,333 changed files. It found no direct #2518 reference or implementation owner; open PRs #2078, #2500, and #2501 have collision-only path overlap. Merged PRs #1334 and #1353 are issue-referenced narrower attempts that repaired rotated-file discovery and event signaling without defining reader or parser completeness. falsifier_or_remaining_gap: An existing pinned implementation would falsify the finding if the reader returned coverage and fragment provenance, every line had a typed outcome, unknown event time and severity remained explicit, the API distinguished readable empty from rejected or incomplete evidence, and console consumers preserved those distinctions. Exact source assertions and the real-parser canary disproved those conditions. The audit did not execute the existing focused suites because their filesystem fixtures create temporary mutable surfaces outside the record-only lane; their assertions were inspected instead. It also did not reproduce the oversized-record HTTP case because doing so requires a writable synthetic log fixture. RED and GREEN byte-level, property, compatibility, consumer, and bounded-resource tests therefore remain implementation obligations. Issue #2447 owns the shared cross-contract; #2513 owns source-sink lifecycle, #2517 owns safe fleet response errors, #2519 owns client gap reconciliation, and #2522 owns aggregate realtime-poller cycle health. Those surfaces require coordinated vocabularies but do not duplicate this reader/parser observation boundary.
impact: A nonempty or partially readable source can appear as a successful empty or quiet result, corruption and schema drift are indistinguishable from intentional filtering, historical undated records can be projected as current, and unknown high severity can be downgraded while still marked as an error. Operators, console consumers, automation, and recovery logic receive neither a coverage denominator nor a trustworthy distinction between empty, incomplete, rejected, and unavailable evidence.
lead_verification_obligations: Re-read the live issue node, title, exact body SHA without a synthetic newline, labels, timestamp, local SSH tracking ref, exact SSH remote main, and every open overlapping pull-request head and fully paginated file list immediately before registry integration or metadata mutation.

Reconcile reader availability, parser outcomes, timestamp provenance, and severity projection with issue #2447 and its current draft foundation without treating that taxonomy work as ownership of reader behavior.

Assign explicit integration boundaries with #2513 for source lifecycle and generation, #2517 for safe JSON and SSE error projection, #2519 for client reconciliation and freshness, and #2522 for aggregate realtime-poller cycle and coverage health.

Require RED and GREEN byte-level tests for leading partial records, multibyte boundary splits, one oversized valid record, later complete records, malformed and non-object JSON, missing fields, and schema drift using reserved synthetic markers only.
Require fixed-memory and fixed-time property or fuzz tests over arbitrary byte offsets, record sizes, newline placement, encoding boundaries, timestamp forms, and numeric and string severity values.

Verify event time remains unknown when absent or invalid, observation time stays separate, ordering cannot promote unknown-time records to current, and no compatibility path silently restores the current-time fallback.

Verify every severity normalization and error-impact field consumes one typed result, unknown values remain fail-visible, and no route, feed, console, or compatibility adapter maps unknown severity to info.

Verify the versioned logs response distinguishes readable empty, nonempty with zero accepted records, incomplete, unavailable, parser-degraded, and oversized observations, including old and new console compatibility behavior.

Verify console log and operator surfaces expose coverage, truncation, rejection classes, observation age, and carried or unavailable state without rendering arbitrary source content or response prose.
Verify parser-loss diagnostics are transition or episode bounded and cannot produce one warning per line, conceal repeated loss, or clear without a fresh complete observation.
Re-scan all open pull-request bodies, references, heads, and changed-file pages before assigning an implementation owner; the three current open overlaps are collision-only, not ownership.

Keep production logs, filesystem locations, live responses, identities, messages, credentials, process or service state, queues, recovery mutation, and deployment outside the draft implementation pull request.
